[RFCS.24.3] **`fact_ids` lists the facts the input asserted, in [RFCS.23.7]'s
order.** Each inlined copy the delivery asserted comes first, innermost first,
then the received fact. A copy that resolved to a live fact asserted nothing and
contributes no handle. A received fact that was a no-op reassertion
([RFCS.6.7]) contributes the handle a `FactAssert` for the same input would
carry. A later
`FactRetract` of any of these facts echoes its handle, as for a `FactAssert`
([RFCS.6.2]).

**Each fact the delivery asserts is its own stream event.** The engine must
emit one `FactAssert` event for each fact in `fact_ids`, in that order, and
each takes the next `seq` ([LFST.5.3]). Each fact's `event_id` derives from its
own event's `seq` ([LFST.5.6]), so no two facts of one delivery share one. The
`ExternalAssert` carries the `seq` of the first of these events. The others are
recorded by no atom of their own, as every stream event of a kind the recording
does not carry is. A replayer delivering the atom emits the same events in the
same order, so every `seq` and `event_id` reproduces.
